memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: He took him outside and said, "Look up at the sky and count the stars - if indeed you can count them." Then he said to him, "So shall your offspring be." - Gen 15:5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God takes Abram outside. Out of the tent, out from under the roof, out where the desert sky blazes with more stars than a man could count in a lifetime. And God says: So shall your offspring be.

There is such tenderness in this. God doesn't just repeat the promise; He gives Abram something to see. He knows we are creatures who need pictures, not just propositions. So He hangs His promise in the sky where Abram can look at it every single night for the rest of his life.

Notice the shift. Abram had been looking down at his empty tent, his childless situation, his ageing body. God says, look up. The circumstances hadn't changed at all - Sarai was still barren, Abram still old. But the perspective changed everything.

Sometimes what we need is not a change in circumstances but a change in what we're looking at. The God who made those uncountable stars is the God who made you a promise. Every clear night for the rest of his life, Abram could step outside and see God's word written across the heavens. What has God said to you that you need to lift your eyes and look at again?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What are you looking down at that God is inviting you to look up from?
- What promise of God do you need to fix your eyes on today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, I have been staring at my circumstances. Take me outside and lift my eyes. Help me look up at Your promises and remember that the God of the stars has spoken over my life.
Amen.
